content.thinking:
Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Certificate:
- number: R60/2000-DK3-16.01
- scheme: A (Certificates of conformity under scheme A... typically OIML-CS scheme A for issuing authority certificates). Actually, older R60 certs predate the OIML-CS scheme naming, but the schema wants "A|B". This is an OIML Certificate of Conformity issued by an OIML Issuing Authority (DK3), which corresponds to Scheme A. I'll put "A".
- project_number: not present. Hmm, DANAK-1916863 is the test report number. Not project number. Omit.
- page_total: 2
- member_state: Denmark
- date_issued: 05 October 2016 → 2016-10-05
- oiml_issuer_id: DK3

Issuing authority:
- name: DELTA
- address_lines: ["Venlighedsvej 4", "2970 Hørsholm", "Denmark"]
- person_responsible: J. Hovgaard Jensen
- person_title: Certification Officer
- phone: +45 7219 4000
- email: legal@delta.dk
- website: www.madebydelta.com
- oiml_issuer_id: DK3

Applicants:
- name: Esit Elektronik Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi
- address_lines: ["Nişantepe Mah. Gelinçiçeği Sok. No.36,", "Çekmeköy,", "34794 İstanbul", "TURKEY"]

Manufacturers:
- same as applicant.

Certified type:
- category: "Load cell"
- type_designations: ["CD"]
- module_designation: "Analog load cell"? The description says "Compression, strain gauge load cell". The R60 module designation... "Analog load cell" is the standard. But don't fabricate — the cert doesn't say "Analog load cell" explicitly. Actually R60 is about load cells; the schema example says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. The certificate doesn't state a module designation explicitly. I'll leave null or omit. Hmm — maybe include "Analog load cell" since strain gauge load cell is analog. But rule 8 says don't fabricate. Omit or set null.
- description: "Compression, strain gauge load cell"

Model family: The Emax row: "25t, 30t, 40t, 60t, 100t" — 5 variants. Also accuracy class C3/C4. So models could be combinations. The matrix table has columns: Accuracy class (C3, C4) with varying values.

Structure: The table varies by accuracy class:
- nLC: C3=3000, C4=4000
- Emax: 25,30,40,60,100 t (same for both)
- pLC: 0.7
- vmin: C3=0.0166 %Emax, C4=0.0156 %Emax
- Y: C3=6000, C4=6410
- DR: C3=0.0033 %Emax, C4=0.0018 %Emax
- Z: C3=15000, C4=27778
- Rated output: 2 mV/V
- Uexc: 5-15 Vac/dc
- Emin/Emax: 0%
- Lim: 150 %Emax
- Tmin/Tmax: -10/+40 °C
- Input resistance: 380 ± 20 Ω
- Output resistance: 350 ± 3 Ω
- Humidity: CH

So model variants: 5 Emax values × 2 accuracy classes = 10 combos. But simplest: model_family with models based on Emax, and model_level entries varying by accuracy class. The accuracy class axis is like a config axis. Hmm.

Option: models = C3 and C4 variants? The varying attributes vary by accuracy class. Emax varies independently (5 values). Full matrix would be 10 models.

I think best approach: model_family.models with model_id like "Emax=25t, C3" etc.? Or keep models as Emax variants and put accuracy-class-varying attributes in config_level with axis "accuracy_class".

The schema for model_level values: {model, value, footnote_markers}. For config_level: {condition, value} plus unit presumably.

Let me structure:

model_family:
- family_name: null (no explicit family name; type CD)
- models: 5 entries "Emax=25t", "Emax=30t", "Emax=40t", "Emax=60t", "Emax=100t"

characteristics:
- type_level:
  - apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7
  - rated_output_sensitivity: 2 mV/V
  - excitation_voltage: {min:5, max:15} V (ac/dc)
  - power supply... excitation voltage Vac/dc → value "AC/DC"? The cell "5-15 Vac/dc" — I'll do excitation_voltage: {min:5,max:15} unit "V", plus excitation_voltage_type: "AC/DC".
  - minimum_dead_load_relative_emin_over_emax: 0 %
  - safe_overload_limit: 150 % with reference Emax
  - temperature_rating: {min:-10, max:40} °C
  - input_resistance: 380 ± 20 Ω → how to express? value could be {min: 360, max: 400}? Or nominal with tolerance: value 380, unit "Ω", plus input_resistance_tolerance: 20? I'll do value: {"nominal": 380, "tolerance": 20}? The schema says value: number | {min,max} | string. Hmm. Maybe value: 380, unit_symbol: "Ω", and a separate characteristic input_resistance_tolerance: 20. Or represent as string "380 ± 20". Better to keep numeric: I'll use value 380 with unit Ω and add "input_resistance_tolerance": 20 with unit Ω. Similarly output_resistance: 350 ± 3.
  - humidity_condition: "CH (No marking)" → value "CH"

- config_level with axis "accuracy_class":
  - max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: C3→3000, C4→4000
  - vmin: C3→0.0166 %Emax, C4→0.0156 %Emax
  - ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 6000 / 6410
  - minimum_dead_load_output_return_dr: 0.0033 / 0.0018 %Emax
  - relative_dr_z: 15000 / 27778

- model_level for Emax: maximum_capacity with 5 values.

Alternatively, treat accuracy classes as models too. The rule 4 example treats Emax variants as models. Accuracy class variation → config_level seems fine per rule 5 ("static vs dynamic weighing" style). Actually accuracy class is more like a model variant... but C3/C4 within same load cell family. I'll use config_level with axis "accuracy_class". Hmm, but the value shape for config_level: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. OK.

Actually, let me reconsider: maybe better to have models be combos? That could be 10 models. That's noisy. I'll go with models = Emax variants and config axis = accuracy class.

vmin values: 0.0166 %Emax — value 0.0166, unit "%Emax"? The unit is % of Emax. I'll use unit_symbol "%Emax" with footnote... Actually rule: "150% of Emax → value: 150, unit_symbol: "%" and a SEPARATE characteristic safe_overload_reference: {value: "Emax"}". Similarly vmin: unit "%", reference "Emax". Hmm, for vmin I could add reference: Emax. The structured value shape doesn't include reference field, but type_level entries are {value, unit, footnote_markers} per characteristics.type_level spec: `<label>: {value, unit, footnote_markers[]}`. Wait — schema says {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers} in rule 2. The layered schema says type_level: `<label>: {value, unit, footnote_markers[]}`. I'll use unit_symbol per rule 2's detailed shape.

For vmin/DR I'll use unit_symbol "%" and separate reference characteristics? That might be noisy. Alternative: unit_symbol "%Emax". I think "%Emax" is clear and concise. Rule 2 example 150% of Emax suggests splitting, but "(Or omit if too noisy.)". For vmin and DR, the %Emax is inherent — Emax varies per model! So vmin in absolute terms varies by model. Keep as %Emax: value 0.0166, unit "%Emax". I'll do that.

Recommendation:
- id: "R60"
- edition: 2000
- amendment: null (omit)
- scheme: "A"? The certificate itself doesn't state a scheme. The schema lists scheme under certificate. For these older certs, hmm. The cert is R60/2000-DK3-16.01 issued by OIML Issuing Authority — that's effectively scheme A. I'll include scheme: "A" in recommendation and certificate? Risk of fabrication. The cert predates OIML-CS but DK3 is an OIML Issuing Authority (equivalent to Scheme A). Many datasets record scheme A. I'll include "A" in both. Actually, safer: certificate.scheme: "A" since it's issued by an OIML Issuing Authority under the conformity scheme. I'll include it.
- accuracy_classes: ["C3", "C4"] — or ["C"]? The cert says "for accuracy class C", and characteristics give C3, C4. I'll list ["C3", "C4"].

Test reports:
- id: "DANAK-1916863", date: 2016-09-12, pages: 35, role: "type_evaluation_report" (test report describing tests). It says "conformity was established by tests described in the associated test report N° DANAK-1916863". Role: type_evaluation_report seems right for R60. I'll use "type_evaluation_report".

Revision history: not present. Omit.

Footnotes: none present.

Matrix_tables: The characteristics table — should I preserve it as a matrix table? It fits into model_level/config_level. The table is 2-D (attribute × accuracy class) plus Emax multi-value. I could add a matrix_tables entry to preserve it. The R137 example emits both matrix_tables and model_level. I'll add one matrix_tables entry "Characteristics" with columns [attribute, symbol, C3, C4] and rows. Rows would be objects with attribute/symbol/C3/C4 values as strings. That could be helpful. Let me do it:

columns: ["attribute", "symbol", "C3", "C4"]
rows:
- {attribute: "type_designation", symbol: null, C3: "CD", C4: "CD"} — hmm type designation spans. Maybe skip.
- {attribute: "max_load_cell_intervals_nlc", symbol: "n_LC", C3: 3000, C4: 4000}
- {attribute: "maximum_capacity", symbol: "Emax", C3: "25t, 30t, 40t, 60t, 100t", C4: same} — messy. Rows values as raw strings okay for preservation.

Actually matrix tables rows should be objects per row. Values mixed numeric/string. Fine.

Let me decide: include matrix_tables with name "Characteristics by accuracy class", columns ["attribute","symbol","C3","C4"], rows as raw-ish entries with numeric where possible:

rows:
1. {"attribute": "accuracy_class", "symbol": null, "C3": "C3", "C4": "C4"}? skip
1. {"attribute": "max_load_cell_intervals", "symbol": "nLC", "C3": 3000, "C4": 4000}
2. {"attribute": "maximum_capacity", "symbol": "Emax", "C3": "25t, 30t, 40t, 60t, 100t", "C4": "25t, 30t, 40t, 60t, 100t"}

Fine.

- temperature_rating_tmin_tmax: {value: {min:-10, max:40}, unit_symbol: "°C"}

Simpler: "input_resistance": {value: 380, unit_symbol: "Ω"} and "input_resistance_tolerance": {value: 20, unit_symbol: "Ω"}. Same for output.
- humidity_condition: {value: "CH", unit_symbol: null} — "(No marking)" means no humidity marking; note that. Could add humidity_condition_marking: "No marking". I'll just record humidity_condition: "CH".

- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 6000/6410

Where do units go in config_level values? {condition, value, unit_symbol}. OK.

model_family:
- family_name: "CD"? The type designation CD could be family name. "explicit family name if any, else null" — CD is the type designation covering all variants, so family_name: "CD" is reasonable. I'll set "CD".

Given config_level captures the class axis and model_level the Emax axis, keeping models as 5 Emax variants is consistent with the R60 example in rule 4 (which only used Emax). I'll do 5 models, and add attributes: {"accuracy_classes": ["C3","C4"]} to each? I'll skip attributes to keep clean.
